overview: The Indo-German Science & Technology Centre (IGSTC) is a joint initiative by the Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India and the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR), Government of Germany. It was established to facilitate Indo-German R&D networking through substantive interactions among government, academia/research system and industries, thus fostering innovation for overall economic and societal developments in both the countries. IGSTC supports various programmes including 2+2 Projects, Industrial Fellowships, WISER, PECFAR, SING, and IGSTC-CONNECT Plus to promote bilateral collaboration in science and technology.
objectives: Facilitate Indo-German R&D networking through substantive interactions among government, academia/research system and industries
Foster innovation for overall economic and societal developments in both India and Germany
Play a proactive role in facilitating participation of industry in joint R&D+I projects
Provide/assist in mobilising resources to carry out industrial R&D+I projects
Promote electronic exchange and dissemination of information on opportunities in bilateral science and technology cooperation
Encourage Public-Private Partnerships (PPP) to foster elements of innovation and industrial application
Nurture networking between young and mid-career scientists and technologists to develop a sense of mutual trust, leadership and entrepreneurship
Develop cooperation through the identification of scientists and scientific institutions of both countries
eligibility: Eligibility varies by programme. For 2+2 Projects: at least one research/academic institution and one industry from both India and Germany are required, with a maximum of six partners (three from each country). Indian academic partners must be public/private non-profit research organisations/institutions of higher education/universities with valid accreditation. Indian industry partners must be companies registered under Indian Companies Act 2013 or LLP Act 2008 or MSME Act 2006 with at least 51% Indian shareholding, R&D setup in India, and in existence for at least three years. German academic partners must be higher education institutions or research organisations providing R&D contributions. German industry partners must be companies in the commercial sector, especially SMEs, with a branch in Germany. For Industrial Fellowships: PhD Industrial Exposure Fellowship (PIEF) – PhD students (science/engineering) enrolled in any research institution/university in India with at least one year of PhD completed, age limit 28 years. Post Doctoral Industrial Fellowship (PDIF) – Postdoctoral researchers/fresh PhDs awarded PhD in science/engineering within 2 years of application deadline, age limit 35 years. For WISER: women researchers/entrepreneurs holding a regular position with minimum 5 years experience in academic/research institutions/industry in India and Germany, no age limit, active employment contract/fellowship valid for more than 4 years from application deadline. For PECFAR: Early Career Researchers with Master’s in Science/Bachelors in Engineering (4 years), regular positions or job contract in academia/research institution/industry, or employment contract with parent organisation while enrolled for PhD, age limit up to 40 years as on application deadline.
benefits: Financial support in the form of grants-in-aid, travel support, fellowship amounts, health insurance, airfare, visa fees, and access to collaborative research networks. Non-financial benefits include access to joint research platforms, technology transfer opportunities, capacity building, networking with academia and industry from both countries, mentorship, and support for commercialization of research outcomes. Specific benefits vary by programme: 2+2 Projects provide grant-in-aid up to Rs. 350 lakhs for Indian partners and Euro 500,000 for German partners over three years. Industrial Fellowships provide €1500/month for PIEF and €2500/month for PDIF, plus round-trip airfare up to €1000 and health insurance up to €100/month. WISER provides travel support for 2-3 visits, research stay of 30-90 days over 24-36 months, and basic project assistance. PECFAR provides fellowship of €2300 per month per fellow (pro rata), travel of €1500 for both Indian and German awardees, and basic project assistance.
financial_support: Financial support varies by programme. For 2+2 Projects: grant-in-aid to Indian partners up to Rs. 350 lakhs and to German partners up to Euro 500,000 for a three-year period. Funding is released yearly as per approved budget and milestones. Indian academic/research partners receive 100% grant-in-aid; Indian industry partners receive up to Rs. 150 lakhs grant-in-aid subject to matching contribution from own resources. German academic/research partners receive 100% of eligible costs in grant form; German industry partners (SMEs) receive grant based on De-Minimis or AGVO rules. For Industrial Fellowships: PhD Industrial Exposure Fellowship: €1500 per month; Post Doctoral Industrial Fellowship: €2500 per month; single round-trip economy class airfare including visa fees and travel insurance up to €1000; health insurance as per actuals with maximum €100/month. For WISER: grant includes travel support for 2-3 visits, research stay of 30-90 days, and basic project assistance (research staff, consumables, minor equipment, overheads, contingency). For PECFAR: fellowship of €2300 per month per fellow (pro rata), travel of €1500 for both Indian and German awardees (single round-trip economy class airfare, visa fees, medical/health/travel insurance, airport transfer, cost of travel for networking visits), and basic project assistance.
application_process: 1. Register on the IGSTC application portal using email addresses. 2. The applicant who starts the application first from the pair is known as the Primary applicant. 3. Primary applicant adds the paired applicant’s details in the application. 4. Paired applicant receives notification and logs in to complete their part. 5. Both applicants jointly access and complete the ‘Paired Project Details’ section. 6. Complete all required sections including financial overview, budget table, activity plan, and upload required documents. 7. Final submission is done by the Primary applicant after all sections are completed by both applicants. 8. Applications must be submitted online via the Application Portal; submissions by other means are not accepted.
required_documents: No Objection Certificate (NOC) from Head/Authorised Signatory of Parent Institution
Proof of Date of Birth (Scan copy of Passport/Aadhar Card)
Proof of Education Qualifications arranged in reverse chronological order
Proof of Current Employment/Fellowship with active contract duration
Recommendation letter from mentor at parent organisation
Two reference letters from established researchers in the field (for PDIF applicants without institutional affiliation)
Completed application form via online portal
Budget table in accordance with Budget Guidelines
Detailed activity plan mentioning objective, work plan, and expected outcomes
Year-wise travel and activity plan for the duration of the project/fellowship
deadlines: Varies by programme: WISER and PECFAR have application window from 1st February 2026 to 31st March 2026 (extended to 2nd April 2026, 12:00 Noon IST/CET). Industrial Fellowships: Application Submission – 1st February 2026 to 31st March 2026 (extended to 2nd April 2026, 12:00 Noon IST). Open Call for Workshops: deadlines twice a year – 31st January and 31st July. 2+2 Projects: annual call for proposals (specific dates vary by year).
implementing_agency: Indo-German Science & Technology Centre (IGSTC), a joint initiative by the Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India and the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR), Government of Germany

caveats: Grant-in-aid assistance is released yearly as per approved budget and milestones; unspent grant may be carried forward subject to IGSTC approval

Assets acquired wholly or substantially by Indian partnering organisations out of IGSTC grant must be maintained and utilized for related scientific activities and cannot be used for unethical purposes
Request for extension in duration of Fellowship shall not be entertained for Industrial Fellowships and PECFAR
Awardee must commence visit within 3 months from date of award letter for Industrial Fellowships
Awardee must submit detailed Fellowship completion report endorsed by host mentor within 4 weeks of completion
Awardees must recognise and acknowledge IGSTC in all online/print documents, communications, reports, publications, conferences, theses, etc.
For 2+2 Projects: maximum six partners (three from each country) allowed in a project; alteration to consortium composition after stage 1 may result in re-evaluation/termination
Financial support to German industry partners is based on De-Minimis or AGVO rules; eligible costs must comply with EU regulations
IGSTC grant is only for supporting monthly fellowship, round-trip airfare, visa fees, and medical/travel insurance (Industrial Fellowships); does not cover other expenses
Applicants must be affiliated to and hold positions in their respective organizations with valid work authorization/contract for the expected duration of the project
